text: Add separate cases, multiply independent steps, subtract the complement.

Addition principle (加法原理): if the ways split into separate cases with no overlap, add the counts of the cases. Multiplication principle (乘法原理): if a choice is made in independent steps, multiply the number of options at each step.

Draw the choices as a tree: a branching step multiplies, separate whole branches add. The usual trap is double counting (cases that overlap) or steps whose options depend on earlier choices; then count the dependent step after fixing the order.

Each rabbit picks a different number from 1 to its own maximum. Give numbers to the most limited rabbit first: when it is rabbit i's turn (0-based), exactly i numbers inside its range are already used, so it has max − i choices. Multiply (P1866).
Sorting makes each step's choices independent of which numbers were taken, only of how many. Take every product % MOD as you go.

Counting attacked cells directly double counts every cell that is hit by both a row and a column. Count the complement instead: a cell is safe exactly when its row has no rook and its column has no rook, (n − r)(n − c) cells by the multiplication principle (P3913).
"Count what you do not want, then subtract" avoids overlaps. Line intersections (P2789) split by how many lines are parallel, and adding up the cases is the addition principle.

A permutation counts ordered arrangements; a combination counts unordered selections. Each combination of k items can be ordered in k! ways, so P(n, k) = C(n, k) · k!.
Pascal's rule: either item n is chosen (then choose k − 1 of the rest) or it is not (choose k of the rest). Filling the triangle (第5章) needs only additions, so no division and no huge factorials.

Store C(i, j) mod k: "divisible by k" means the value mod k is 0, and Pascal's rule works mod k too. Up to 104 queries then read a 2D prefix sum in O(1) each instead of rescanning the triangle (P2822).

Only words with strictly increasing letters get a code, ordered by length and then alphabetically. Code of a word = 1 + (number of valid words before it): all shorter words, C(26, len) for each length, plus same- length words that are smaller at the first differing position (P1246).

After fixing a smaller letter ch at position i, the remaining L − i − 1 letters are any increasing choice from the 26 − ch letters above ch: C(26 − ch, L − i − 1). Stars-and-bars style splitting (P2638) is another "choose positions" count.

Key points to memorise
1. Separate cases: add. Independent steps: multiply.
2. Overlaps are hard to count: count the complement and subtract.
3. Steps that depend on earlier choices: order them (sort) so only how many, not which, matters.
4. n! arrangements; P(n, k) = n!/(n−k)!; C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!).
6. Pascal: C(n, k) = C(n−1, k−1) + C(n−1, k); works mod any k.
7. Many range queries: 2D prefix sums over the triangle.
8. Rank of an object = 1 + count of smaller objects, position by position.
